recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-17771; future detailed national ICD variant maintenance should occur in the terminology source of truth rather than by reintroducing the retired core ICD variants page.
issue_request: FHIR-17771 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 Vocabulary technical correction reporting that paragraph 4.2.11.2 had the ICD-10-NL and ICD-10-DE OIDs reversed; the issue identifies ICD-10-NL as 2.16.840.1.113883.6.3.2 and ICD-10-DE as 1.2.276.0.76.5.409.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly names FHIR-17771, consistent with the Jira comment that the problem was already fixed. Historical source shows the ICD page already listing the correct NL and DE values in 2017, followed by GF#13123-era changes that removed the explicit German ICD-10 system/OID details from core after German community feedback.
additional_context: Current publish.ini references source/sid-icd-10.html and source/terminologies-systems.html. The old source/icd.html page that contained the national variant table was deleted by FHIR-35933, while current source delegates ICD-9/10 details to HL7 Terminology. A later ICD URI-column correction, FHIR-41305, is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. Current build-scoped core source does not contain the reversed old ICD-10-NL/DE OID row, and current in-repository references found outside the retired page label 1.2.276.0.76.5.409 as ICD-10-DE and 2.16.840.1.113883.6.3.2 as ICD-10-NL.

related_jiras.note: Later corrected the ICD-9/10 URI column in source/terminologies-systems.html and is already audited on the combined branch.
Deleted the old source/icd.html page that contained the historical national ICD variant table.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive technical correction reporting that ICD-10-NL and ICD-10-DE OIDs were reversed in paragraph 4.2.11.2.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final issue request and the correct target values, with Jira noting the problem was already fixed.

evidence_items.summary: The current ICD-10 source page only defines http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10 as the international ICD-10 system and cites WHO.
evidence_items.learned: The current build-scoped ICD-10 page no longer contains the old national variant OID table that FHIR-17771 targeted.

evidence_items.summary: The current terminology systems table delegates ICD-9/10 details to the HL7 Terminology Using ICD page.
evidence_items.learned: Current core source does not publish the reversed ICD-10-NL/DE OID values and instead points to terminology-maintained guidance.

evidence_items.summary: The 2017 ICD page introduction listed ICD-10-DE as 1.2.276.0.76.5.409 and ICD-10-NL as 2.16.840.1.113883.6.3.2.
evidence_items.learned: The source history already contained the correct values before FHIR-17771 was filed.

evidence_items.summary: GF#13123-era commits removed the explicit German ICD-10 OID/system from source/icd.html after ICD-10-DE feedback.
evidence_items.learned: These commits explain the Jira comment that the reversed listing had already been fixed by removing or correcting the problematic German entry.

evidence_items.summary: FHIR-35933 deleted source/icd.html and adjusted source/terminologies-systems.html.
evidence_items.learned: The old ICD variants table is no longer part of current core source, so FHIR-17771 has no remaining core source target.

evidence_items.summary: Community discussion confirmed the ICD-10-NL OID as 2.16.840.1.113883.6.3.2 and recorded German feedback that core should not maintain the ICD-10-GM URL/OID details.
evidence_items.learned: The community trail supports the historical source edits and reveals no conflicting current requirement for core source.
